## The problem

Materials researchers characterize electrospun nanofiber gels by hand-tracing fibers in SEM images. That is slow, analyst-dependent, and covers only a few dozen fibers per sample, so comparisons between fabrication conditions are weakly powered.

## Approach

Perona-Malik anisotropic diffusion, morphological top-hat, fixed threshold combined with Canny edges, and skeletonization. Junctions are found with 17 hit-or-miss kernels. Segments meeting at a junction are paired by most anti-parallel direction and merged with union-find. Arc length, PCA orientation and a tangent-correlation persistence length are then computed per fiber. The interactive app provides crop, scale-bar and parameter controls, plus CSV/PNG/PDF export. Prototyped in the lonespear/aerogel Colab notebooks (2024).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Turns a manual measurement into a repeatable instrument, so a lab can test whether a fabrication condition (e.g., high-alignment vs 2:1 alignment gels) changes fiber alignment and length, with known measurement error. This is not yet demonstrated: no validation or between-condition comparison exists.
:::

## Limitations

- No ground truth: never compared against manual tracing, synthetic fibers of known geometry, or an established tool (DiameterJ, FiberApp, ImageJ Ridge Detection).
- Physical calibration is collected in the UI but never applied; all outputs are in pixels.
- Persistence-length estimator uses exp(-s/Lp) instead of the 2D worm-like-chain form exp(-s/2Lp) and a 20-pixel lag window; in simulation it returns about 2x true Lp and saturates near 140 px on skeleton-like chains.
- 'Lambda' = log(Lp)/L is not dimensionless and changes with the unit choice.
- Arc length on pixel skeletons carries a +3-5% diagonal-step bias; greedy point ordering adds a heavy upper tail (p90 +44-77% for curvy fibers in simulation).
- Orientation mean/SD computed linearly on axial (0-180 deg) data; rose diagram is mirrored relative to image coordinates.
- Results depend on about 9 hand-set thresholds with no sensitivity analysis; fibers cut by the image border are length-censored; 2D projection understates true length.
- Exercised only on a handful of images from one lab; junction pairing is unvalidated at crossings and bundles.

## Tools

Python, OpenCV, scikit-image, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn (PCA), NetworkX, pandas, Matplotlib/Seaborn, Streamlit
